messages:
sales-jordan: Orchid Health (dedicated pool 'orchid-prod-1') reported throughput drop after deploy this morning. p50 ~40ms, p95 jumped from 210ms -> 1.8s, now seeing request queueing. Their support ticket: https://support.redwood/12345. They flagged it's impacting SLAs. Can oncall triage? :eyes:

oncall-ryan: looking. link to their trace + logs?

sales-jordan: attached in ticket - will paste key errors: "batch queue length exceeded capacity". They also included client-side traces showing retries. Request rate steady ~120 rps.

ops-bot: deploy-bot finished rollout to dedicated-pool 'orchid-prod-1' commit abc123def at 2026-03-19T09:12Z.

maya-s: I can pull metrics. Querying p95 over last 30m for pool 'orchid-prod-1'.

maya-s: metrics: p95 tokens latency: 1.8s at 09:30, p50 42ms. Queue length metric: avg 18, spike to 60 during rollout.

samir: is this a model change or infra? Deploy-bot shows commit, but what's in that commit? @infra-elaine can you check kernel/quant changes? 

infra-elaine: commit abc123def touched model-serving configs -> upgraded torch from 2.1.0 -> 2.2.0 and adjusted default max_batch_size from 64 -> 128. Rollout likely increased batching and introduced queueing for some tail workloads.

oncall-ryan: ah - default batch growth could push longer tails. For Dedicated we usually preserve max_batch_size per-customer. Why did config change global?

infra-elaine: it was an infrawide optimization for throughput on small models; missed a targeted override. PR 4821.

maya-s: reproducing locally: with max_batch_size=128, p95 jumps on short-context requests because batching waits longer for filling batches. With 64 it's much better.

samir: can we patch orchid pool to set max_batch_size=64 and restart workers as hotfix?

infra-elaine: yes. I'll patch config and rollout a safe restart to pool 'orchid-prod-1'.

ops-bot: rolling config update to dedicated-pool 'orchid-prod-1' (change max_batch_size=64) - 5 nodes at a time.

maya-s: after first 5 nodes, p95 dropped back to 220ms. Queue length normalized.

sales-jordan: orchid confirms SLA is recovering and appreciates the quick action. They asked why this wasn't detected in canary.

product-lina: note for roadmap: need stronger per-customer config guardrails and canary coverage for Dedicated pools. Add to backlog? This is customer impact and SLA risk.

oncall-ryan: created INC-2345 (https://incidents.redwood/INC-2345) to track incident. Action items: 1) infra patch to revert global default (PR 4823). 2) product to add per-customer default overrides + canary tests (ticket PROD-987). 3) add regression alert on batch-induced p95 spike (SRE-542). Assigned owners: infra-elaine, product-lina, eng-sre-marc.

product-lina: we'll scope the backlog item: min viable - enforce per-pool overrides + a pre-deploy check; stretch - automated detection to prevent changing live per-customer defaults.

samir: timeline? Orchid wants RCA and timeline for permanent fix.

product-lina: aiming for hotfix rollback PR by EOD, backlog item in next sprint, RCA doc by tomorrow.

sales-jordan: filing customer-facing summary and ETA. :thumbsup:

oncall-ryan: closing triage here. If regressions reappear, reopen INC-2345 and ping #pager.

ops-bot: incident INC-2345 created by oncall-ryan at 2026-03-19T10:05Z.

[reactions: :white_check_mark: oncall-ryan, :eyes: sales-jordan]
